newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Firm amid tight supply expectations.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Firm amid tight supply expectations.

text.p: Expectations of lower fuel oil exports from South Korea and Kuwait kept Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices firm on Monday, traders said.
The 180-cst grade was heard traded at $100 per tonne for May 17-21 lifting, unchanged from last Thursday's trading level, traders said.
"Interest from local buyers should continue this week over fewer supplies from Kuwait and South Korea next month," said one trader.

Kuwait's domestic summer demand will cut down its fuel oil exports while South Korea is expected to export only about five to six cargoes of fuel oil in May, lower than its average levels due to maintenance turnarounds, traders said.
"There are fundamental reasons for prices to rise," another trader said.
Fuel oil swaps were slightly softer over concerns that the recent physical support would not last through May.
May swaps were last heard at $97.50/$98.50 compared with $98.00/$98.75 last Thursday.
However, most traders expected supplies to tighten in the second half of May and they said such anticipations should support prices.
Recent fresh tender demand from Taiwan and India has also helped sentiment although the demand was so far considered regular, traders said.

State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has issued a tender to buy 30,000 tonnes of 3.5-percent sulphur, 180-cst grade fuel oil for May 15-19 delivery, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Bombay, traders said. The tender closes on May 1 and will be valid for one day.
IOC has another outstanding tender closing on April 24 to buy 30,000 tonnes of fuel oil for May 6-10 delivery, c-and-f Bombay on the Indian west coast.
Taiwan has issued a six month tender to buy up to two 38,000 tonne cargoes per month of fuel oil between June and November.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
